takeaway: Cerebral perfusion pressure = MAP − ICP. With MAP 60–160 mmHg and ICP about 10 mmHg (CPP 50–150 mmHg), autoregulation maintains sufficient blood flow.

lines.text: This equation is MAP minus ICP.
lines.say: This equation is mean arterial pressure minus intracranial pressure.

lines.text: MAP is the mean arterial pressure.
lines.say: M A P is the mean arterial pressure.

lines.text: ICP, the intracranial pressure, is subtracted from it.
lines.say: I C P, the intracranial pressure, is subtracted from it.

lines.text: The difference is the cerebral perfusion pressure.
Normally, MAP is between 60 and 160 mmHg, and ICP is about 10 mmHg,
lines.say: Normally, mean arterial pressure is between sixty and one hundred and sixty millimetres of mercury, and intracranial pressure is about ten,

lines.text: giving a CPP of 50 to 150 mmHg.
lines.say: giving a cerebral perfusion pressure of fifty to one hundred and fifty millimetres of mercury.

lines.text: In that range, autoregulation maintains sufficient blood flow.
So if MAP falls or ICP rises, the perfusion pressure falls.
lines.say: So if mean arterial pressure falls, or intracranial pressure rises, the perfusion pressure falls.
